subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should maintainers accept this Unix kill-tree leader-check behavior once the branch is rebased onto current main and current detached cleanup callers are re-audited?
rationale: The code path controls gateway and child-process termination; the patch looks like the right bug fix, but changing the shared default and resolving current-main conflicts requires owner acceptance of compatibility and availability tradeoffs.

options.title: Rebase and land after caller audit
options.body: Carry the helper change onto current main, add detached:true to every current detached-spawn cleanup path including newly added siblings, rerun focused cleanup tests, and proceed if CI is clean.

options.title: Keep the old contract
options.body: Reject the shared default change and instead require every unsafe caller to pass detached:false or detached:true explicitly, accepting continued caller-cooperation risk.

options.title: Pause for a core process owner rewrite
options.body: Hold this PR and design a narrower process-cleanup API that makes spawn-time process-group state unrepresentable at the call site.

recommendation.title: Rebase and land after caller audit
recommendation.body: Carry the helper change onto current main, add detached:true to every current detached-spawn cleanup path including newly added siblings, rerun focused cleanup tests, and proceed if CI is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame routes the live process cleanup helper and several current caller surfaces through this author, making them the best available current-code owner for the merge-risk decision.
